Latest Update: AlphaProof Code: How AI Agents Formally Verified Signal's Encryption in Four Weeks

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that formal verification — mathematically proving that software does exactly what it claims — has long been the gold standard of software security.
  • On November 10, 2026, Google DeepMind published AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI framework that completed a comparable feat in four weeks with a team of five researchers — and none of them wrote a single line of proof code.
  • It has been revealed that the target was libsignal, the open-source reference implementation of the Signal protocol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that formal verification — mathematically proving that software does exactly what it claims — has long been the gold standard of software security. It is also notoriously expensive. Verifying the seL4 microkernel took twenty person-years. Verifying the CompCert C compiler took six. For most production software, that cost is simply out of reach.

On November 10, 2026, Google DeepMind published AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI framework that completed a comparable feat in four weeks with a team of five researchers — and none of them wrote a single line of proof code.

It has been revealed that the target was libsignal, the open-source reference implementation of the Signal protocol. Signal's cryptography protects billions of conversations in Signal, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Google Messages. The protocol has two main components: the PQXDH handshake, which establishes a shared secret between two parties (including a post-quantum key encapsulation step), and the Triple Ratchet, which derives a fresh encryption key for every single message.

Prior formal verification work on Signal stopped at the design level — proving that the protocol specification was sound. AlphaProof Code went further: it proved that the compiled machine code of libsignal satisfies those security properties. The proofs are stated over the actual AArch64 binary, not the Rust source. That distinction matters because real-world vulnerabilities often hide in the gap between a correct design and its implementation.

The security properties established include:.

The framework divides formal verification the way a research team would, separating the work into two distinct phases.

Humans decide what to prove. A specification-writer agent works with researchers to translate Signal's security goals into formal Lean theorems. Reviewer agents critique each draft. Human experts approve the final specifications. This is the trusted part of the system — the specifications cannot be automatically checked, so they require human judgment.

According to recent reports, the key insight here is that the specifications are small: about 27,000 lines of trusted Lean code. The proofs, by contrast, are enormous.

Industry observers note that once specifications are approved, teams of 40 to 80 autonomous agents — powered by Gemini 4 Carbon — take over. An orchestrator divides the proof work into subtasks. Proof workers tackle individual lemmas. An architect designs and revises the high-level proof decomposition. An integrator merges verified proofs into shared library modules and removes duplicate lemmas.

Every proof is checked by Lean's kernel, which serves as the ultimate arbiter. If an agent makes a logical error, Lean rejects the proof. The agents' work is untrusted by design — only the kernel's verdict counts. A gatekeeper agent accepts a proof only when Lean confirms it proves exactly the specification the human approved.

The result: 6.3 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof code, generated in four weeks.

According to recent reports, to validate that the specifications were strong enough to catch actual flaws, the team reintroduced two previously fixed bugs from libsignal's history: a "Weak state" bug and a "Small subgroup" bug. In both cases, AlphaProof Code produced a machine-checked proof that the buggy version was insecure. The system found no new flaws in the portions it checked.

This is a meaningful sanity check. A formal verification system that cannot detect known bugs provides weak assurance. The fact that AlphaProof Code caught both historical vulnerabilities suggests the specifications are capturing the right properties.

The technical paper is explicit about scope. The verification covers one-to-one chats in a specific build of libsignal, not the full Signal application. Group messaging, key generation, and the Signal app itself are out of scope. The proofs also assume that low-level cryptographic primitives — SHA-256, AES-CBC, Kyber1024 — behave as specified; they do not verify those primitives themselves.

Signal's CTO Ehren Kret acknowledged the result while noting its limits: "As AI-driven security threats grow, having the core Signal protocol rigorously verified with automated theorem proving gives us even greater confidence that our code delivers on its privacy guarantees.".

Recent findings suggest that perhaps the most interesting observation from the paper is about where the difficulty now lies. Swarat Chaudhuri, one of the lead researchers, told The Register: "We really believe that the next frontier is not going to be proof but specification.".

It has been revealed that when proofs become cheap to generate, the bottleneck shifts to deciding what to prove and writing precise formal statements of those properties. Specification writing requires deep domain knowledge — understanding what "forward secrecy" means in the context of a specific protocol, and translating that into a Lean theorem that captures the right attacker model. That is still a human-intensive task, and it is where most of the four weeks went.

Industry observers note that this has practical implications for how formal verification might scale. If AI agents can handle proof generation reliably, the limiting factor becomes the supply of people who can write good specifications — a different skill set from traditional proof engineering.

Recent findings suggest that alphaProof Code is a step toward making formal verification economically viable for production software. The seL4 microkernel verification took twenty person-years and required the code to be written with verification in mind. AlphaProof Code verified pre-existing, unmodified production code in four weeks.

It has been revealed that the framework is not yet a general-purpose verification tool. The Signal project was carefully scoped, and the team had deep expertise in both cryptography and formal methods. But the trajectory is clear: AI agents are compressing the cost of formal verification by orders of magnitude.

Industry observers note that deepMind has open-sourced the verification artifacts — the specifications, proofs, and AArch64 semantics — for community review. This matters because the value of formal verification depends on the community being able to audit the trusted computing base. Open-sourcing the work invites scrutiny of the 27,000 lines of trusted specifications, which is exactly where errors would be most consequential.

For practitioners, the near-term takeaway is not "run AlphaProof Code on your codebase." It is that the cost curve for formal verification is bending, and the skills that will matter most — writing precise, auditable specifications of security properties — are worth developing now.

Primary source: AlphaProof Code blog post and technical paper by Google DeepMind (November 10, 2026). Additional reporting from The Next Web (November 12, 2026).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark 1x-27B is Saanora's most capable model: 84.7 on GPQA Diamond, a 262K-token context window, tool calling, image input and adjustable reasoning effort. It speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API, so if your code already uses the OpenAI SDK, switching is two lines: the base URL and the model name.

According to recent reports, mark thinks before it answers. The answer is in choices[0].message.content; the thinking comes back separately in choices[0].message.reasoning (billed as output tokens). Set how hard it thinks with reasoning_effort: low, medium or high.

It has been revealed that $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0.60 per 1M output tokens, paid from prepaid credit. Top-ups start at $5. One key and one balance work for every model on the API.

One note: when Mark has been quiet for a while, the first request can come back as 503 model_warming_up with a Retry-After header while it starts. Retry after that time; those requests aren't charged.

Docs: api.saanora.com. I'd love to hear what you build with it.

Breaking: Wendell Berry on Where Our Gone Loved Ones Go

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (377 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Themarginalian

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • To love is to sign a contract with loss.
  • Industry observers note that when two people have loved one another, each has become embedded in the marrow of the other’s being and both have had a profound experience that cannot be unhad even when the slender thread of grace between them is severed, by death or disenchantment.
  • Sources indicate that death, of course, is only one species of loss, one way our loved ones can leave us.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To love is to sign a contract with loss. To love anyway is both the great tragedy and the great triumph of life.

Industry observers note that when two people have loved one another, each has become embedded in the marrow of the other’s being and both have had a profound experience that cannot be unhad even when the slender thread of grace between them is severed, by death or disenchantment. “No one you love is ever dead,” Hemingway wrote in his moving meditation on death and the meaning of life disguised as a letter of consolation to a bereaved friend.

Sources indicate that death, of course, is only one species of loss, one way our loved ones can leave us. We can also be left in life, left behind, left wondering where love goes when it goes. At its most discomposing, abandonment can feel like a living death.

Industry observers note that all deep loss has one thing in common: It opens an absence so acutely felt it kidnaps us from presence, takes us away from our own lives and their insistent, inconvenient, sacred ongoingness. In memory or in fantasy, we end up refugees from reality, ceding the only thing that is ever ours for the keeping: the living moment. In all missing, we miss life.

That is what the achingly missed Wendell Berry (August 5, 1934–August 31, 2026) explores in this gasp of a poem, originally published in the November 17, 2025 problem of The New Yorker:.

THE LOVED ONES by Wendell Berry.

The loved ones we call the dead depart from us and for a while are absent. And then as if called back by our love, they come near us again. They enter our dreams. We feel they have been near us when we have not thought of them. They are simply here, simply waiting while we are distracted among our obligations. At last it comes to us: They live now in the permanent world. We are the absent ones.

Couple with physicist Richard Feynman’s extraordinary love letter to his wife written long after her untimely death, then revisit Wendell Berry on creativity and love and his timeless antidote to despair.

— Published November 8, 2026 — https://www.themarginalian.org/2026/11/08/wendell-berry-loved-ones/ —.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bedow adapts Coopâs circular plate into asymmetrical packaging design for Nordic household goods, pairing color arcs with technical linework.

Half of the twelve AA batteries on Coopâs alkaline carton are real metal cells; the rest are printed gray silhouettes continuing straight across the tray. That small visual cue explains the whole system. When Coop rolled out its latest Nordic identity, its non-food essentials still needed a clear voice across kitchens, bathrooms, and laundry rooms. Batteries, detergents, cotton pads, and paper rolls sit far from groceries, so Bedow couldnât rely on appetizing food cues. The studio kept the circular plate and recipe logic from the main Coop range, then pushed that plate into an asymmetrical layout built around technical graphics and straightforward utility.

In a recent development, color coding and crisp linework drive the shelf navigation. On the alkaline battery packs, bright yellow marks AA, orange signals AAA, cobalt blue identifies C cells, and olive green codes 9V â each color filling a cropped corner arc against cool gray card stock. A fine matrix of plus and minus signs traces polarity along the border while oversized size letters and the green Nordic Swan Ecolabel sit right beside the die-cut window. Toothpaste tubes run on the same asymmetrical logic. Across the 75 ml White, Classic, and Fresh variants, bold vertical type locks inside a curved blue or mint zone while radiating dotted arcs echo the plate rim and twin circular icons summarize brushing guidance. On the toothbrush blister cards, geometric line patterns back the adult Flexy and Classic brushes before opening up into tiger and coral illustrations for the Kids and Junior handles.

That packaging design stretches cleanly across softer formats too. Translucent green and blush-pink arcs wrap directly over the embossed rolls of Dry & Strong kitchen paper and Nice & Soft toilet paper, pairing fine white contour lines or feather sketches with clean roll-and-layer icons. It doesnât break on small cartons either. Cotton Buds boxes tuck two paper-stick swabs right into the curved blue plate beside neat 100% Cotton and 200 PCS circles. Over in dishwashing, the Machine Powder and All-In-1 cartons shift into deeper navy, cyan, and emerald arcs layered with sparkling glassware and circular function badges. Every item in this packaging design reads as Coop on a crowded aisle, yet nothing left beside a sink or inside a utility drawer feels borrowed from the pantry.

See the full project on Bedowâs website.

The best Black Friday deals we’ve already found

In a recent development, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The countdown to Black Friday is on, and many discounts have already arrived. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until Friday, November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a wide variety of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected later this week.

Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to revision this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

Sony’s last-last-gen noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and a 10-band EQ, delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

Lego’s miniature bonsai trees can bring a sense of calm to even the most cluttered home. Building each tree — whether it be the black pine, the ginkgo, or the lilac-adorned wisteria — is designed to be a mindfulness practice in itself, centering your giftee as they go. They also make for a great piece of decor once finished, adding a touch of zen to any desk or shelf.

According to recent reports, rechargeable AA batteries are handy, until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in a easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

In a recent development, sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Sources indicate that the Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

It has been revealed that anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

According to recent reports, fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Industry observers note that no one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

According to recent reports, the Nintendo Switch 2 has 256GB of storage, but that won’t get you very far if you’ve built up a medium-sized digital game library. Samsung’s P9 256GB microSD express card doubles the console’s available storage.

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Sources indicate that despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

Sources indicate that JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

It has been revealed that hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Recent findings suggest that govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

Industry observers note that birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

It has been revealed that bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.

Headspace makes it easier to build mindfulness into your everyday life, whether you’re looking to manage stress, improve focus, or get a better night’s sleep. An annual subscription gives you access to hundreds of guided meditations, breathing exercises, and other tools for beginners and experienced users alike.

It has been revealed that the Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets, thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”.

Industry observers note that garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

According to recent reports, the Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost human-like navigation, tackling high-pile rugs, and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

It has been revealed that the Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

Nothing’s first pair of over-ear headphones feature a retro transparent design and high-end features like active noise cancellation, spatial audio with head tracking, and plush ear pads. They also feature a paddle button that allows you to control music playback. Read our review.

It has been revealed that amazon’s 12.3-inch Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs Android with access to the Google Play Store, unlike the firm’s Fire tablets. It also features built-in Alexa Plus integration, a dedicated Kindle reading mode, and up to 16 hours of battery life. Read our hands-on impressions.

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

TP-Link’s smart smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms, and lets you set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

It has been revealed that google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds feature crisp sound quality, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

Sources indicate that roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.

Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

The latest entry in the long-running survival horror series returned in 2026, with two different styles of gameplay (tense first-person and guns-blazing third-person perspectives) via its dual protagonists. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that the latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.

In a recent development, the major difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

Industry observers note that the Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.

It has been revealed that with a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

According to recent reports, the Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for fresh consumers. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some latest features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.

In a recent development, it’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches).

Recent findings suggest that the water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

It has been revealed that LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they fit seamlessly into any major smart home platform. Best of all, the smart features come at a price that makes buying multipacks more affordable than other brands.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.

It has been revealed that donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that whether you primarily drive a car, motorcycle, or a bicycle, the one thing in common with all three modes of transport is the need for a well-inflated tire. This rechargeable 150psi inflator might just save you from a flat (or from being dangerously close to one) when you least expect it.

It has been revealed that google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging.

In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

In a recent development, A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

Sources indicate that glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

Sources indicate that this innovative fresh smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It will also work with the new Aliro standard and be compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.

Few plants are as festive to have around the house during the holidays as poinsettia. Lego’s 608-piece recreation stands 8 inches tall, includes a “woven-basket” flowerpot, and — unlike the one you undoubtedly received as a gift in the past — requires absolutely no maintenance.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

It has been revealed that the Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

Recent findings suggest that the Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

It has been revealed that the last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Patch, November 23rd: Added a wide selection of fresh deals, including those for Amazon’s Alexa Photo Frame, Anker’s Universal Charger, and the Nintendo Switch 2.

#149085. The 9 Best Chain Restaurant BLTs, According To Customer Reviews

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2046 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

The 9 Best Chain Restaurant BLTs, According To Customer Reviews

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A good BLT is elegantly simple, a masterclass in culinary economy.
  • These details make it hard for chain restaurants to nail a great BLT.
  • Cook Out has built a restaurant empire on selling comfort foods that you'd find at a backyard barbecue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A good BLT is elegantly simple, a masterclass in culinary economy. With this sandwich, nothing is superfluous, nothing is forced. Instead, each ingredient works in unison to create an unmatched harmony of taste, temperature, and texture. Whether you're craving a light nosh or a substantial sit-down lunch, somehow a BLT always fits the bill. And because of its pared-down composition, every element has a chance to shine on its own. However, this also means there's no place to hide mistakes. If the tomato is a bit mealy, the bacon slightly chewy, or the bread a tad soft, it can throw off the entire sandwich.

These details make it hard for chain restaurants to nail a great BLT. They serve thousands of meals every day, and each individual order exposes them to a world of criticism and critique. To save yourself from a sub-par sandwich, you need to know which chains are executing a quality BLT. And this list hopes to do just that, featuring a handful of fast food chains and restaurants that are dishing up both familiar renditions and inventive interpretations of this classic sandwich. To find the best, I searched social media, roundups, and other online forums to uncover which chain restaurants are doing the BLT justice.

Cook Out has built a restaurant empire on selling comfort foods that you'd find at a backyard barbecue. From hush puppies to corn dogs to some of the best fast food milkshakes in the country. But it also offers a fun take on the classic BLT. While most people judge the sandwich's quality by the crispness of its lettuce, the juiciness of its tomato, or the number of grains in its whole wheat bread, Cook Out takes a different approach: speed, price, and efficiency.

It has been revealed that these sandwiches are essentially BLT sliders: compact handhelds you can devour quickly and without a tummy ache. Despite their size, photos show you get a decent amount of each ingredient packed onto the tiny hamburger bun. And at a time when value is a particularly tasty quality, the fact that these mini sandwiches cost between $2 and $3.49 (depending on your location) makes them even more delicious. "They are ridiculously cheap," remarked one customer on Facebook. "Less than two bucks..." On Reddit, the feelings are mutual, with another commenter posting, "The BLTs are the unsung hero of Cook Out." Apparently, not all heroes wear capes; some wear bacon.

In a recent development, sonic is another chain known for its nostalgic, carhop-inspired food. It has all the munchies you crave late at night: tater tots, root beer floats, breakfast burritos — really, the menu covers the gamut. But the restaurant is best known for its selection of classics, including the BLT. While some BLTs are light and dainty, Sonic's BLT Toaster is on the heftier side, perfect if you're craving something not greasy but still substantial enough to keep you full throughout the day. The sandwich isn't such a departure from classic BLTs, but everything just feels, well, bigger. The hand-sliced tomatoes, fresh lettuce, and trio of meaty bacon strips all come sandwiched between two thick slabs of buttery Texas toast.

In a recent development, customers, say that they love the BLT, with one YouTuber noting it's "crispy, crunchy, and yummy." And speaking of breakfast, Sonic's BLT Toaster is frustratingly elusive. It's not discontinued, but it doesn't always appear when ordering online. A workaround is to get the Grilled Cheese and just add bacon, lettuce, and tomato. Or you can just ask for it specifically if ordering in person.

According to recent reports, potbelly knows how to put together a quality sandwich, and as far as chain sub shops go, it should be in the conversation with Jersey Mike's, Jimmy John's, and Firehouse Subs — at least that's what people are saying on the Reddit threads. However, like most fast food empires, quality varies by location. Still, a good Potbelly sandwich is as solid as any, typically well-stuffed, with a great ratio of condiments and toppings.

This same formula and attention to detail that make its Italian sub a customer favorite also show up in its BLTA (the "A" stands for avocado). Texturally, it's a terrific blend of creamy, cool, crispy, and crunchy, and unlike the more value-friendly fast food restaurants, the sandwich is assembled with a little more care. Customers note that the avocado is freshly sliced, the bread is crusty and substantial, and the pepper-crusted, applewood-smoked bacon is the best of any sandwich chain. "Potbelly makes an amazing BLT," claims one happy diner on Instagram. "...the lettuce and tomato are fresh and refreshing. The bacon is peppered, which adds a great flavor. The bread-to-ingredients ratio is amazing. Solid BLT 9/10.".

According to recent reports, jason's Deli is more than just a deli. It has more than 200 locations, mostly in the South and Midwest, which is why it probably doesn't get the national acclaim it deserves. But Jason's makes some incredible food that's unlike anything else you'll find at other fast food restaurants and casual chains: giant baked potatoes, massive slow-cooked brisket sandwiches, and a bottomless salad bar that might just be the best in the country.

It has been revealed that its version of a BLT — aptly named the Bigger Better BLT — is no slouch, either, although it's sure to ruffle the feathers of BLT purists. Why? Well, the sandwich is stuffed with a few extra letters from the alphabet. Obviously, it includes the standard bacon, lettuce, and tomato — albeit in greater quantity than average —plus slices of avocado and a freshly cracked fried egg, all piled on two slices of multi-grain wheat. In general, customers are impressed by the amount of bacon and the overall sandwich composition. "This is my favorite menu item from here," noted a Redditor after posting a glam shot of their sandwich.

According to recent reports, from its famous #13 Original Italian to the Big Kahuna Cheesesteak, Jersey Mike's knows how to put together a sandwich. The chain takes the same thoughtful approach with its #1 BLT. Our sister site, Chowhound, ranked it the tastiest chain restaurant BLT around, citing the quantity of ingredients and textural harmony as key reasons for its success.

Jersey Mike's doesn't do anything special with its BLT. No bells and whistles or novel additions; it just nails the basics, with a precise ratio of tender tomato, refreshing shredded lettuce, crispy bacon, and a good mayonnaise (and some oil and vinegar or chopped pepper relish if you get it "Mike's Way"). The bread cradles the ingredients so nothing gets too soggy or, worse, falls apart.

On a Facebook post dedicated to the BLT debate, one person commented, "Jersey Mike's is the only place I will go for 'fast food' subs!" Others agree, with another poster noting, "...this was wayyyy good [...] I only wish I got extra bacon, but there was a good amount." And while everyone appreciates a simple sandwich, many customers say their customizations improve the taste, adding everything from tangy banana peppers to spicy chipotle mayo to your standard slice of American cheese.

Five Guys is known for its juicy burgers, thick milkshakes, and an unnecessary abundance of fries, but the fast food restaurant also makes one of the best BLTs of any national chain. However, Five Guys created some confusion among its fan base by formally "launching" the BLT sandwich just a few months ago, even though many loyal customers say it's more of a relaunch, given that it's been available for more than a decade.

Industry observers note that regardless, the sandwich is now available nationwide, which is good news for anyone who loves a BLT that doesn't skimp on the B. The sandwich is served on a sesame seed burger bun, but the applewood-smoked bacon is piled so high that it's about the thickness of a double (or triple) stacked cheeseburger. "They PILE the bacon on those BLTs," commented one Redditor, "...it's unlike any BLT I've ever had because of the sheer volume of meat." Facebook owners have similar feelings. Overall, customers view it as an underappreciated alternative to the major sandwich chains, especially for the price, which is a few dollars less than Five Guys' standard burger. On a Facebook post comparing BLTs from other chains, one person commented: "Should have gone to Five Guys. That's the GOAT BLT.".

Cheba Hut has been around since 1998, with its original location satisfying hungry students from the Arizona State University campus. Its menu reflects the playful, somewhat frenzied, college-kid mentality. Sandwiches are bold and inventive, with names and ingredient combinations that would make Panera Bread blush. Its version of the BLT — the Sensi Kush — has a traditional foundation of bacon, lettuce, and tomato, but it also includes a few, dare we say, dank touches that set it apart from your other basic sandwich chain, specifically a drizzle of sriracha honey, fresh avocado, and a buttery blanket of provolone.

Sources indicate that is this genius or BLT blasphemy? Based on customer reviews, it is most definitely the former. "I love a good BLT but I really love the Sensi Kush BLT from Cheba Hut! The honey sriracha sauce is 100," noted one Facebook user, along with a pic of their sandwich. Customers on Instagram agree, with one commenter writing, "The sensi kush is fire," while another on Reddit said, "I love Cheba Hut! I think they make the best BLT I've ever had.".

First Watch is a sizable chain with nearly 700 locations across mostly the eastern half of the United States. The restaurant offers a diverse lineup that emphasizes freshness and ingredient quality over speed and cost. At First Watch, there's something for everyone: lemon ricotta pancakes, power breakfast bowls, Benedicts, elaborate, lunch-y salads, etc., but when it comes to sandwiches, its BLT(E) is one of the best.

It has been revealed that it pairs your typical BLT with two over-hard eggs (can't have messy yolks getting everything soggy) and Monterey Jack cheese — all on its artisan whole-grain bread. BLT snobs may scoff at the extra ingredients, but the bread, along with the sandwich's overall engineering, is as good as you'll find at a local cafe or diner. The portion is sizable, bordering on two portions-worth. The sandwich's flavor takes people by surprise as well, with it being filling and tasty while not weighing you down. One Instagram post noted, "I enjoyed the BLTE [...]. It was so good. [...] I think I might start orderind sandwiches at First Watch each time I go." For something even more out there, try First Watch's BLT Benedict, which is basically an open-faced BLT sandwich topped with poached eggs and hollandaise.

Sources indicate that celebrity endorsements don't mean everything, but John Oliver (the star of HBO's Last Week Tonight) once publicly stated to his friend Stephen Colbert that his favorite sandwich is none other than a Wawa BLT. But this shouldn't be such a shock. Wawa is famous for its reasonably priced subs and sandwiches, and its BLT doesn't disappoint (at least when the bacon is properly cooked). While a Tasting Table ranking didn't put the BLT at the top of the list, the author still praised the sandwich, saying it was "perfectly built...nicely slathered with creamy mayo and stuffed with strips of bacon, shredded lettuce, and sliced tomato.".

In a recent development, some chains (even a few on this list) are guilty of — every so often — skimping on ingredients. Not Wawa. Its sandwiches are pretty stuffed. One Facebook user said, "The BLT hyperfixation is in fullllllll effect." Even if you do end up with a thin sandwich, the staff will gladly remake it to your liking. Another ordering tip: Wawa recently moved the BLT from the "cold" to "hot" sandwich section, which has caused some confusion amongst customers over fears that it had been discontinued.

To find the chain restaurants with the best BLTs that delivered on taste, price, and overall value, we dug through dozens of online forums, social media video reviews, and taste tests from within the past year. In the end, this list represents some of the best BLTs you can find, based on photos, reviews, and customer feedback.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that early Unix was available through inexpensive source-code licenses because a 1956 antitrust settlement kept AT&T out of the commercial computer business [6].
  • Industry observers note that defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) also valued Unix's source-code availability.
  • Industry observers note that but AT&T's breakup in 1984 opened the way for it to sell Unix commercially.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that early Unix was available through inexpensive source-code licenses because a 1956 antitrust settlement kept AT&T out of the commercial computer business [6]. Some early licenses cost just $99 [1].

Industry observers note that defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) also valued Unix's source-code availability. That was why it chose BSD Unix over DEC's VMS for building the Internet [1].

Industry observers note that but AT&T's breakup in 1984 opened the way for it to sell Unix commercially. AT&T abruptly raised the price from $99 to $250,000 [1].

Industry observers note that BSD still required an AT&T license. When fees rose, some companies wanted its networking code separately.

How can I get just BSD'sTCP/IP and vi source code?

AT&T's raised the fees.Users want just ournetworking code and tools.

Let's release ournetworking codeand tools separately.

Anything goes, huh? Well, we don't want to putrestrictions on people like AT&T does.

BSD's networking releaseis finally here.

They'll mail you a tapefor $1,000. Or download itfree by FTP. We can evenchange and redistributethe code without royalties.

Professor, the networkingrelease is selling well.

Grants, tape sales...Development's fundedfor a while.

Professor, why don't we make a version of BSDthat doesn't require an AT&T Unix license?

We can't keep depending on AT&T.We've already changed much of the kernel.It's the tools and C library we need to rewrite.Can we do it rapidly?

Let's try. With help fromoutside contributors, we canrewrite the AT&T code.

CSRG decided to rewrite AT&T's tools and C library. With help from outside contributors, most of the code was rewritten in eighteen months.

With most of AT&T's Unix code removed, a completely free BSD Unix was finally released in June 1991. The source was still available on tape for the $1,000 copying fee, or as a free download by FTP.

Industry observers note that CSRG founded a organization called BSDi to sell BSD Unix commercially. The University of California also began selling BSD Unix in the early 1990s. An advertisement claimed it was 95% cheaper than AT&T Unix. That did not go down well with AT&T.

In April 1992, AT&T subsidiary USL sued BSDi. UC Berkeley was added to the lawsuit later.

I thought we'd removedall the AT&T code...What's this?

AT&T's suing us for distributingUnix code without permission.

That's absurd. System V includesour virtual memory, TCP/IPand vi code.

The BSD side filed a countersuit against AT&T.

In February 1994, the two sides agreed that each could sell Unix, provided CSRG removed some remaining AT&T Unix code.

It's the same code...Wouldn't want his job.

If I could have installed BSD Unixon my Intel 386 PC,I wouldn't have needed to write Linux.

That wraps up our six-part story of BSD Unix!

It has been revealed that browning the milk solids brings out a deep aroma and adds layers of "baked" flavor to your confections, but it's easy to go overboard and end up burning them. You know brown butter is done when the solids start to brown but the fat remains golden, giving the whole thing a caramel color that isn't quite as dark as milk chocolate. You can use room-temperature butter for this, though cold butter will also work as long as you heat it evenly.

The same way using regular butter rather than browned butter is a missed flavor opportunity, simply dumping it into a batter and stirring away makes you lose out on better texture and taste. Bringing your butter to the right temperature, creaming it with the sugar, and adding subsequent ingredients in the right order may seem inconsequential, but they make a noticeable difference.

  • According to recent reports, A classic grilled cheese is a thing of both beauty and comfort.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

According to recent reports, A classic grilled cheese is a thing of both beauty and comfort. And of course, a simple sandwich such as this is open to interpretation, with many putting their own spin on it, like making it Swiss-style with raclette cheese or switching up the grilling process by using an air fryer, like Ree Drummond. But there's an easy addition you can make to your next grilled cheese that will make it even tastier (and it's not mayo or butter, though you can certainly use either): It's store-bought caramelized onion dip.

It has been revealed that when spread onto the bread and covered in cheese, then warmed through in a hot pan, caramelized onion dip brings a burst of flavor and a compelling texture to the sandwich. Of course, it's definitely savory, but the caramelized onions also introduce a subtly sweet element to grilled cheese, creating a flavor sensation that is much more interesting for your taste buds. Meanwhile, the dip melts into the cheese, adding to the creaminess, while the onions introduce a little toothsome variety to chew on, beyond the softness of the filling and the crispness of the bread.

In a recent development, trader Joe's Caramelized Onion Dip is one great store-bought option, and it's part of the store's regular lineup, so you should be able to find it year-round (unless it has sold out). Whole Foods also sells a version under its 365 brand, which Amazon Prime members can shop for on Amazon.

If you have the desire to take things a step further, you might try a mix-in or two that can elevate the taste of the dip (and therefore, your entire sandwich). That might include some dried cranberries, which can help draw out the aforementioned sweetness of the onions, creating an even bolder contrast in your salty grilled cheese. You also might play to the richness and crumble up some crisp bacon into the base. Or enhance the savory, aromatic vibes by adding both thinly sliced scallions and chives.

Now, if you're having trouble finding caramelized onion dip at your grocery store, you could always make your own, though cooking down the onions properly can be laborious. If standing over your stove for 45 minutes doesn't appeal to you, Ina Garten cuts down on the time by using a larger pot, which allows the onions to cook more evenly and efficiently. But if you'd rather skip the cooking altogether, you might find the adjacent caramelized onion jam on store shelves. This won't be as creamy as the dip, but it will still impart that same rich, savory, and slightly sweet flavor, so it's a decent substitution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Interval Type pairs Sugarspark display typography with 14-style Sugarswift text across 22 retro-futurist Latin and Cyrillic cuts.

It has been revealed that both versions of Interval Typeâs mid-century brand roll call sit right beside each other in the specimen set. Sony, Braun, Polaroid, Atari, Olivetti, and Pierre Cardin run twice across identical lists. On the white scanline sheet, Sugarspark strips the spurs off every lowercase n and r, slicing between names with sharp diagonal slashes. Switch to the dark companion poster, and Sugarswift puts those vertical stems back in, trading slashes for four-point stars. Paris founder Ilya Naumoff rolled out Interval Type in 2022 as what he called âstill a bit of an experiment.â Four years later, built by a two-designer team, this release splits 1960s and 70s space-age typography into two paired families totaling 22 Latin and Cyrillic styles.

Industry observers note that sugarspark doesnât hide its candy-like streak. According to TYPE01, the display half chases what Interval Type calls ânaive modernismâ from early video game console covers, product manuals, and space-age packaging. Its forms pull from three clear touchstones. ITC Bauhaus, alongside Blippo and Pump, supplies wire-bent monolinear curves and spurless n and m arches. ITC Kabel brings angled terminals, an eccentric lowercase g, and a diagonally sliced e alternate that shaped Sugarsparkâs snaky S â while Herb Lubalin and Tom Carnaseâs Avant Garde Gothic anchors the uppercase W and tightly locking ligatures. Every quirk demonstrates up fast on the typography plates. On the pink Night Stereo card, that snaky S, quirky lowercase g, and spurless r sit above a yellow Cyrillic pill and a hairline green ABCDE strip. On the 650pt ÃP poster and roller-skate ÃÃ specimen, neighboring capitals share stems and diagonals under solid-dot or hollow-ring umlauts.

Display tricks like those wouldnât hold up in dense paragraphs, which is where Sugarswift steps in. Its specimen lays out 14 text styles across seven upright-and-italic weight pairs lined up along the bottom edge. Put Sparkâs Newly introduced Shift sheet next to Swiftâs Neue Shrift plate and the change is immediate: Sugarswift widens character widths, restores spurs on n, r, and u, drops the rounded Bauhaus capitals, and straightens the hairline arrows. Wrapped in CRT scanlines, mirrored disco skates, and a poolside cat in yellow sunglasses under âA Sweet Spark of Retro Kitsch,â the typography isnât pure nostalgia. Itâs a working split between giant 650pt ligatures and compact bilingual text that stays legible when scaled down.

Tate’s Bloomsbury group exhibition throws fresh light on early British enthusiasm for Van Gogh

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1295 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tate Britain’s exhibition Vanessa Bell & Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury, which opened yesterday (12 November), emphasises how early 20th-century British artists were inspired by Van Gogh.
  • Vanessa Bell (1879-1961) and Duncan Grant (1885-1978) lived together for more than 50 years in a very Bloomsbury fashion, each having other lovers.
  • As the Tate show’s curator, Thomas Kennedy, points out: “When Bell and Grant were doing newly introduced and exciting things, individuals like Van Gogh—who were creating something wildly different from other artists of the time—were very much an inspiration for them.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tate Britain’s exhibition Vanessa Bell & Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury, which opened yesterday (12 November), emphasises how early 20th-century British artists were inspired by Van Gogh.

Vanessa Bell (1879-1961) and Duncan Grant (1885-1978) lived together for more than 50 years in a very Bloomsbury fashion, each having other lovers. The Bloomsbury group, named after the London quarter where they lived in the early 20th century, began as an informal collective of progressive artists, writers and intellectuals.

As the Tate show’s curator, Thomas Kennedy, points out: “When Bell and Grant were doing newly introduced and exciting things, individuals like Van Gogh—who were creating something wildly different from other artists of the time—were very much an inspiration for them.”.

Bell and Grant were both also very close to the art critic Roger Fry, who in 1910 curated the pathbreaking London exhibition Manet and the Post-Impressionists, inventing the term Post-Impressionism. This show introduced Van Gogh to a British audience.

Vanessa Bell’s portrait Roger Fry (1912).

© National Portrait Gallery, London.

According to recent reports, as so often with the Bloomsbury group, sexual relationships were complex and intertwined. In 1907 Vanessa had married the art critic Clive Bell, but it was always an open marriage. Two years later she started a relationship with Duncan Grant, producing a daughter, and they then continued to live together.

In a recent development, duncan Grant, however, was homosexual, having numerous lovers, including a male cousin and Vanessa’s brother. To add to the complications, Vanessa later had a brief relationship with Roger Fry. The quip about the group was that they were “living in squares [in Bloomsbury], painting in circles and loving in triangles”.

The Bloomsbury relationships may seem bewildering to outsiders, but the key point to bear in mind with the current Tate exhibition is that Bell and Grant shared a home for over 50 years. Initially they lived in London, and, from 1916, partly at Charleston farmhouse in rural Sussex.

According to recent reports, it proved to be an enduring artistic partnership. They influenced each other, and they, in turn, were influenced by modern European artists, such as Van Gogh, along with Paul Gauguin, Paul Cezanne, Henri Matisse and Pablo Picasso.

The impact of Post-Impressionism: Duncan Grant's The Mantelpiece (1914) and Vanessa Bell's Still Life on Corner of a Mantelpiece (1914).

Recent findings suggest that grant, who studied art in Paris in 1906, may have then come across the work of Van Gogh. What is more certain is that Bell discovered Van Gogh in 1909, in a group exhibition at London’s Latest Gallery, which included a single painting by the Dutchman. She once described it as “a lovely little Van Gogh of flowers in a jug”.

Sources indicate that the still life had been lent by Thomas Fisher Unwin, a London publisher who, with his wife Jane, had in 1896 been the first Briton to buy a Van Gogh after the artist’s death. This was a flower still life, probably one with a black background which has always been in private collections.

Van Gogh’s Bouquet of Flowers (summer 1886).

private collection (formerly Galerie Schmit, Paris).

Post-Impressionism and Provence.

Sources indicate that but what was most influential for Bell and Grant was Fry's first Post-Impressionist exhibition in 1910. Including around 30 works by Van Gogh, it was the first chance for Londoners to see more than an odd painting by the artist.

This was a heady time for the Bloomsbury group. Bell later recalled: ”That autumn of 1910 is to me a time when everything seemed springing to a latest life - a time when all was a sizzle of excitement, new relationships, new ideas, different and intense emotions all seemed crowding into one’s life.”.

Catalogue of the second Post-Impressionist catalogue (1912), co-designed by Bell, Grant and Fry.

Bibliothèque de l'Institut National d'Histoire de l'Art, Jacques Doucet collections.

Recent findings suggest that in 1912 both Bell and Grant had paintings in Fry’s second Post-Impressionist exhibition. They also co-designed the catalogue with Fry, and Bell helped hang the show. This time there was only a single Van Gogh, but it was again the Fisher Unwin flower still life, which Bell had known from four years earlier.

Recent findings suggest that bell, Grant and Fry all loved the south of France, where Van Gogh had also worked, and they visited regularly from the 1920s. Fry helped a friend buy a farmhouse in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, just a few hundred metres from the asylum where Van Gogh had stayed in 1889-90. On one occasion Grant visited Bell, who had bought a house just outside Cassis, on the Mediterranean coast. Grant described the surrounding landscape as “far more extraordinary than St Remi [sic]”. Both artists were well aware of Van Gogh's connection with Provence.

Duncan Grant’s South of France (1920).

© Tate. Photo © Tate (Joe Humphrys).

How then did Van Gogh’s art inspire Bell and Grant? They never set out to simply imitate his style, but were nevertheless powerfully influenced by his work and that of the other Post-Impressionists. The two British artists began to paint with heightened colours, simplified forms and strong lines.

The links can also be seen in individual pictures. Bell’s View into a Garden (1926, Bolton Library & Museum Services) includes two empty chairs, which were probably a reflection of Van Gogh’s pair of paintings of his own chair and the armchair of Gauguin (the picture of his own chair had been bought by London’s National Gallery three years earlier, so would have been well known to Bell).

According to recent reports, the critic Frank Rutter described Bell’s Chrysanthemums (1920, Tate, although not in the current exhibition) as “undoubtedly influenced by Van Gogh”. Its dark background echoes the Van Gogh still life which Bell had seen some years earlier.

Decades later, in 1946, Grant wrote to Bell about visiting a Van Gogh exhibition in Copenhagen, “a splendid show”. He added: “I really feel that artists should resist to the death having their works reproduced in colour. It really has been the death of Van Gogh. It’s only when one sees the originals that one realises what a very lovely & personal colour sense he had… I really do not believe in his madness as an artist at all.” Van Gogh remained in the minds of the couple for the rest of their lives.

Martin Bailey is a leading Van Gogh specialist and special correspondent for The Art Newspaper. He has curated exhibitions at the Barbican Art Gallery, Compton Verney/National Gallery of Scotland and Tate Britain.

Martin Bailey’s recent Van Gogh books.

Industry observers note that martin has written a number of bestselling books on Van Gogh’s years in France: The Sunflowers Are Mine: The Story of Van Gogh's Masterpiece (Frances Lincoln 2013, UK and US), Studio of the South: Van Gogh in Provence (Frances Lincoln 2016, UK and US), Starry Night: Van Gogh at the Asylum (White Lion Publishing 2018, UK and US) and Van Gogh’s Finale: Auvers and the Artist’s Rise to Fame (Frances Lincoln 2021, UK and US). The Sunflowers are Mine (2024, UK and US) and Van Gogh’s Finale (2024, UK and US) are also now available in a more compact paperback format.

His other recent books include Living with Vincent van Gogh: The Homes & Landscapes that shaped the Artist (White Lion Publishing 2019, UK and US), which provides an overview of the artist’s life. The Illustrated Provence Letters of Van Gogh has been reissued (Batsford 2021, UK and US). My Friend Van Gogh/Emile Bernard provides the first English translation of Bernard’s writings on Van Gogh (David Zwirner Books 2023, UKand US).

To contact Martin Bailey, please email vangogh@theartnewspaper.com.

Please note that he does not undertake authentications.

What Happier People Tend To Believe About Others

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Org

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.
  • A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.
  • Trusting others is linked to greater happiness and life satisfaction, a review involving over 2.5 million people finds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.

A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.

Trusting others is linked to greater happiness and life satisfaction, a review involving over 2.5 million people finds.

Happier people also tend to become more trusting over time.

The link between trust and happiness is slightly stronger in children, adolescents and older adults, possibly because supportive relationships are especially important at these ages.

Trust may help meet the need to belong by making it easier to build relationships in which people feel supported and secure.

The research combined almost 1,000 findings from studies involving people aged six to 84.

The analysis examined how trust related to everyday emotions, including happiness and sadness, as well as people’s overall satisfaction with their lives.

Greater trust was consistently associated with better wellbeing.

The association was somewhat stronger among children and adolescents than among young and middle-aged adults, and stronger among older adults than young adults.

Trust may matter more at ages when people are building close relationships or becoming more dependent on others.

For younger people, learning whom to trust is part of building meaningful friendships and supportive social networks.

In later life, people may prioritise a smaller circle of close relationships and depend more on others for support.

The researchers distinguished between trust in familiar people, trust in people generally and trust in institutions.

The first involves confidence in someone known personally, such as a partner, friend or relative.

General trust involves expectations about people more broadly, including strangers, while institutional trust concerns organisations such as governments, banks and the police.

All three were associated with better wellbeing, but trust in familiar people revealed the strongest connection.

Trust may support wellbeing partly because close relationships require a willingness to be vulnerable.

Expecting someone to respond with care can make it easier to seek help, cooperate and maintain a supportive connection.

These relationships may satisfy the basic psychological need to feel connected to others and cared for in return.

Trust could also provide a broader sense of security and predictability, making the social world feel more dependable.

This may help explain why trust was slightly more closely related to overall life satisfaction than to positive or negative emotions.

Life satisfaction reflects a broader assessment of how life is going, whereas emotions can fluctuate with immediate experiences.

The relationship also worked in the other direction, with greater wellbeing predicting more trust later.

One proposed explanation is that emotions influence how people interpret the world around them.

Feeling happy may encourage more positive perceptions of other people, while anxiety may draw attention towards threats and uncertainty.

Trust and wellbeing could therefore reinforce each other, with supportive expectations helping people feel better and positive feelings making trust easier.

The wider social environment mattered too, with a stronger connection between trust and wellbeing in countries where people were generally more trusting.

A trusting outlook may be more beneficial when the people around us are dependable.

Simply encouraging someone to trust more overlooks the behaviour of the people and institutions receiving that trust.

Professor Catrin Finkenauer, study co-author, mentioned:.

“But trust can’t be forced—it has to be earned.”.

The findings therefore highlight the importance of honesty, reliability, transparency and fair treatment in relationships and institutions.

“When we build trust, we also support mental health and stronger communities.”.

The study was published in the journal Psychological Bulletin (Bi et al., 2025).

According to recent reports, psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. Bjork and I like ours topped with pickled jalapenos or crispy onions, and the girls, of course, like them “plain” on a squishy white bun.

Sources indicate that I always always make these with what we call Ranch Potatoes, which are the truly the delight of my life. In our house, it’s not Sloppy Joe’s if there’s no pile of crispy, buttery Ranch Potatoes on the side. 🙂.

Regarding diced onion, pepper, or garlic in the Sloppy Joe filling: this recipe has none. Everyone I cook for enjoys these the same (or even more?) with an uncluttered texture and just a few hits of garlic and onion powder instead, which makes this whole thing even faster and easier.

Recent findings suggest that my youngest requested this as her birthday meal this year. Hope you like it as much as we do!

Leave it sitting undisturbed for a few minutes so that it develops a nice golden crust.

Garlic powder, onion powder, beef bouillon, ketchup, and BBQ sauce!

It has been revealed that add some water as needed to make the mixture loosen up and turn a bit glossy. It can just hang out until you’re ready to eat.

When you’re close to eating, pop your potatoes in the oven.

Once they’re roasty toasty, add a knob of butter and some ranch seasoning. Toss to combine. (If you don’t have ranch seasoning, just use melted butter, fresh garlic, and dill. UNREAL.).

Load it onto a soft bun – we love this with ranch potatoes and green beans!

Recent findings suggest that easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. We love these with Ranch Potatoes!

White garlic sauce (for dipping, as shown in the video): Whisk 1/4 cup mayo, 1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, 1 clove grated garlic, 1-2 tablespoons water, and salt to taste.

In a recent development, making Ahead: The meat mixture is ready to go right after you add the ketchup and BBQ sauce, but I usually like to let it simmer for 30-60 minutes to really caramelize around the edges and deepen in both flavor and color.
